title: Geopolitical Daily
email_subject: Xi tells Putin ties 'firm as a mountain'
preheader: The two meet in Shenzhen a day before a three-way summit with Trump.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Wednesday, November 18, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 1 update on stories you're following and 6 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: Xi and Putin meet in Shenzhen before Trump three-way summit
stories.why_important: Chinese leader Xi Jinping met Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen and called Russia ties 'firm as a mountain,' one day before a three-way summit with Donald Trump. The meeting puts China at the center of diplomacy among major powers. Kyiv and Europe fear the three leaders could shape Ukraine's fate without them.
stories.what_overlooked: No fixed agenda for Thursday's summit is public, and Washington has not said what it will offer. The lack of terms makes any deal hard to verify.
stories.prediction: Thursday's three-way meeting will end with a joint statement or no statement; a Ukraine deal would show whether Kyiv was sidelined.

stories.story_title: Iran denies dirty-bomb report as Trump warns
stories.why_important: Iran denied a CNN report that it planned a dirty-bomb or chemical attack in Washington. President Trump said the US takes the claim 'very seriously.' US officials said they had no evidence Tehran had decided to act. The report could push the US toward new military action.
stories.what_overlooked: The White House said there was no credible threat to US territory. That caveat has received less attention than Trump's warning.
stories.prediction: US intelligence or the White House clarifies whether the threat is credible within 72 hours; a public assessment would show if the report changes policy.

stories.story_title: Israel's parliament elects Netanyahu opponent as speaker
stories.why_important: Israeli lawmakers elected Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, as speaker with 66 votes to Likud's 52. The vote weakens caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as Eisenkot tries to form a government. Police and Shin Bet face claims they helped Netanyahu challenge election results.
stories.what_overlooked: Le Monde reports that no evidence has emerged for Netanyahu's claims of 'massive fraud' in Arab lists. Even so, police raided and detained people over them.
stories.prediction: Eisenkot will announce a coalition within 72 hours or ask for more time; failure would raise the chance of another Israeli election.

quick_hits.text: The US criticized Ukraine's long-range strikes on Russia; Germany's defense minister called it 'quite a stupid thing' and Britain defended the strikes.
Democrat Mary Peltola won Alaska's Senate seat, giving Democrats a 56-44 majority after the final midterm race was called.
The NSA's classified communications network went down for hours; the agency blamed temporary degradation during scheduled maintenance.
A US judge sentenced Asif Merchant, a Pakistani man, to over 27 years for plotting to kill Trump at Iran's request.
Ukraine struck the Crimea bridge for a second day, while Russia hit Kyiv's bridges, in what data suggested was the war's largest drone attack.
A new report says Bangladesh sends officials accused of human rights abuses to serve as UN peacekeepers, while the UN documents abuses at home.
